newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were generally stable in lethargic late trading on Friday.

"I haven't sold anything yet since the last deal on Wednesday at 43.00 (U.S. cents/lb) fob Padang for September shipment. I am afraid prices will decline again next week as our attention is still on Thailand," said one trader in Padang, West Sumatra.
Thailand's decision to adopt a managed float system that effectively devalued the currency has further dampened the bearish market sentiment in Indonesia's rubber markets.
Indonesian traders said the move meant that Thailand would sell rubber at cheaper prices.

"The overall market sentiment is still bearish and we haven't hear of any fresh deals today. We are hoping that INRO (the International Natural Rubber Organisation) will intervene to prop up prices, but we are not sure," said another trader.
Traders said offer prices were quoted at 44.00 fob Medan, 43.375 fob Palembang, 43.50 fob Surabaya and 43.25 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
